claims.text: Expected response: reticulocytosis USU after 1 wk; in responders Hb starts rising after 1 to 2 wks (~1 g/dL by 14 days); anemia should be corrected w.in 2 months.
claims.quote: Reticulocytosis usually occurs after 1 week, and Hb begins to rise after 1 to 2 weeks with an ~ 1 g/dL increase at 14 days in responders (2). Anemia should be corrected within 2 months.

claims.text: OD: up to 20 mg/kg elemental Fe = ⍉toxic; > 60 mg/kg can cause severe toxicity.
claims.quote: Up to 20 mg/kg of elemental iron is not toxic, 20 to 60 mg/kg is mildly to moderately toxic, and > 60 mg/kg can cause severe symptoms and morbidity.

claims.text: Severe toxicity (met acidosis, shock, severe gastroenteritis or serum Fe > 500 mcg/dL): IV deferoxamine, w IV hydration.
claims.quote: Patients with severe toxicity (metabolic acidosis, shock, severe gastroenteritis, or serum iron level > 500 mcg/dL [89.5 micromol/L]) are treated with IV deferoxamine to chelate free serum iron. Deferoxamine is infused at rates up to 15 mg/kg/h IV, titrated until hypotension occurs. Because both deferoxamine and iron poisoning can decrease blood pressure, patients receiving deferoxamine require IV hydration.

claims.text: Radiopaque tablets on XR: whole-bowel irrigation; activated charcoal doesn't adsorb Fe.
claims.quote: If radiopaque tablets are visible on abdominal radiograph, whole-bowel irrigation with polyethylene glycol 1 to 2 L/h for adults or 25 to 40 mL/kg/h for children is done until no iron is visible on repeat abdominal radiograph. Administration via nasogastric tube may be necessary to deliver these large volumes and care must be taken to protect the airway; intubation may be necessary (see Tracheal Intubation). Gastric lavage is usually not helpful because vomiting tends to empty the stomach more efficiently. Activated charcoal does not adsorb iron and should be used only if other toxins were also ingested.
